 3. rep i (a representation of the widened divFunctorAff at each parameter) -- the R2 divisor-
    representability target. Rows: ddr.divrep (+ u2, abel-widened); the old chart-typed divFunctor route is not the current carrier.

RIDERS THAT ARE NOT SEPARATE OBLIGATIONS, both established by retraction below:
 * hD (LocallyOfFiniteType) is a rider on antecedent 3, proved via
   rep.uniqueUpToIso -- unconditional, not contingent on the carrier divRep
   returns.
 * hcpt IS the JacobianData.quasiCompact field, so dat-glue and dat-j name ONE
   obligation. Qualification (r4, I-1162): the half carrying that -- the mpr
   direction -- has been the producer's own implementation since 07-27
   (JacobianDataCharts.lean:216); the new content is the mp direction, which
   shows the identification cannot be undone. hcl still has no producer, so
   nothing there is discharged.

r4 REPRICING -- WITHDRAWN BY ITS AUTHOR, same session. I wrote here that the chart
parameter n is pinned to the genus by chi_moduleKSheaf UNCONDITIONALLY, so
abel-noninj owed no "we are at n = g" argument and its n > g branch was

chi_moduleKSheaf CONVERTS chi = 1 - n into n = genus C, it does not SUPPLY
chi = 1 - n. With n free and no chi hypothesis the goal FAILS, and it still fails
with a representation at n in scope. My probe had hchi as a binder, so it measured
the conversion (I-1177).
   THE STANDING PRICE is ajcr-p2's: n > g is unreachable for a chart built on a
producer IN THIS TREE, because each such producer carries an hchi at its own
index. That is a claim about producers and a lane must keep them in view.
Whether an inhabitant exists at n != genus C is an OPEN inhabitation question
about DivRepAffinePullback -- mixedParamChart typechecks at arbitrary nn.
abel-noninj's live target is unchanged: the carve question, does DivScheme g
contain points where H^1 fails to vanish.

SORRY COUNT IS NOT DEBT HERE: 17 sorries, all in Challenge.lean (15, the
statement-only north star) and Pic0ThetaCocycle.lean (2). A naive count reads

ANSWER TO THE COSTING QUESTION, unchanged this round: none of the three closes

================================================================================
HISTORY FOLLOWS -- corrections in reverse chronological layers.
================================================================================

*** hcpt CLAUSE RETRACTED 2026-07-29 (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006), refuted by ajcr-p4 (I-1007)
within minutes of my writing it. THE DEGENERACY OBSERVATION IS REAL; MY CAUSAL READING WAS
CONFOUNDED. ***

I wrote, in the self-correction below, that "hcpt is NOT an independent gate but a CONSEQUENCE of
coverage", inferred from hcpt being free at iota := PEmpty while all content sat in the
IsLocallySurjective instance. p4's refutation is decisive and I verified its pivot myself (EXIT=0):
PEmpty IS FINITE. So freeness of hcpt there is explained by the FINITE-INDEX route
(JacobianData.ofCharts with per-chart compactness at an empty cover), with coverage contributing
nothing. A degenerate index attributes to whichever hypothesis happens to vary, and I varied the
wrong one.

WHAT p4 MEASURED, more useful than my claim was: feeding the openCover route directly,
(glueData hf).openCover.compactSpace fails on EXACTLY ONE goal --
Finite (glueData hf).openCover.I0. Not chart compactness, not the cover being a cover, not
coverage. Add [Finite iota] plus per-chart CompactSpace and the same term closes. p4 also applies my
own I-0978 correctly: a failing synthesis measures the instance graph, so this does NOT prove hcpt
independent of coverage -- it shows no route in scope derives it, and the single gap on the
available route is INDEX FINITENESS, which the class-indexed atlas provably lacks.

CONSEQUENCE, and it strengthens the item rather than weakening it: DO NOT schedule "derive hcpt
from coverage". The two honest options are the ones the tree names -- a finite atlas, or the Abel
image (JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage out of a quasi-compact DivScheme). The class-indexed atlas
needs the second, and PRICING IT is the unowned work. Row AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-j points there.

*** SELF-CORRECTION 2026-07-29, SAME SESSION (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006, after a fresh-context
review of my OWN correction below). THE FOURTH ITEM IS NOT AN ANTECEDENT AT ALL -- IT IS A RIDER
ON antecedent 3, AND I PROVED IT RATHER THAN ARGUED IT. Read this before the arithmetic
correction that follows; that correction's CONCLUSION survives but its UNIT OF PRICING was wrong. ***

WHAT I GOT RIGHT AND WHAT I GOT WRONG. Right: the count was 3-of-3 where the goal needs more, the
"derived, not assumed" sentence was misleading, and ajcr-p4's discharge is real. WRONG: I priced
hD : forall i, LocallyOfFiniteType (D i).hom as a FOURTH INDEPENDENT ANTECEDENT that p4 removed,
and justified its cheapness by the CARRIER the divRep lane happens to return today
(locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom). That argument is CONTINGENT -- it would need re-measuring
if divRep ever returned a different object.

THE UNCONDITIONAL FACT, PROBED, `lake env lean` EXIT=0, axioms [propext, Classical.choice,
Quot.sound]: if divFunctor C pi n is representable by D and by D', and D'.hom is locally of finite
type, then D.hom is. Three lines -- e := rep.uniqueUpToIso rep', e.hom.left is IsIso via
Over.comp_left on hom_inv_id, then rw [<- Over.w e.hom] and infer_instance.

SO hD IS AN INVARIANT OF THE FUNCTOR AT THE PARAMETER, not a property of the chosen carrier. No
producer of rep can choose a D that fails it, and none can be blamed for one that does. The right
place for it on this board is as a RIDER ON THE rep ROW (divrep), not as an item of its own -- a
row that lists it separately INFLATES the antecedent count, which is the same error in the
opposite direction from the one I was correcting.

THE ANTECEDENT LIST OF THE GOAL, corrected again and now on unconditional grounds:
 1. hf = IsChartUniv. OPEN (chart-restrict, ajcr-p1).
 2. Zariski-local surjectivity of Sigma.desc. OPEN (dat-b, ajcr-p2).
 3. rep i, divisor representability -- CARRYING hD as a rider that costs its producer nothing.
    OPEN (divrep.u2).
 4. quasiCompact. OPEN, and see the degeneracy note below, which reprices it.

AND A DEGENERACY THAT REPRICES quasiCompact, measured on the same pass. At iota := PEmpty EVERY
explicit input of jacobianDataOfMixedParamCharts is free -- hf/hdeg/V/hD/m/Z/nn by PEmpty.elim,
and hcpt free too because an empty family glues to an EMPTY space (IsEmpty => CompactSpace by
inferInstance). ALL the content sits in the single IsLocallySurjective instance. The output is
nevertheless NOT vacuous, and that was also probed (EXIT=0, same axioms): that instance at PEmpty
implies False, because JacobianData.rep yields a point of J over every test (homEquiv.symm 1)
while J.left is empty. TWO CONSEQUENCES: (a) the assembly is sound and falsifiable, so nothing
here is a HasDivFunctor-style vacuity; (b) hcpt is NOT an independent gate of this shape but a
CONSEQUENCE of coverage -- and any future "hcpt discharged" measured at a small atlas measures
nothing at all.

ALSO CORRECTED, and it is a false absolute I repeated from p4's file: "the only declaration in
Picard/ whose conclusion is LocallyOfFiniteType is locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom". There are FIVE
non-local ones plus 38 local re-derivations; the omitted ones include the very instance
(DivSchemeQProj.lean:199) that Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean imports and cites to make hD free, so the
absolute is refuted by that file's own closing section. THE DEFENSIBLE FORM, which is what a board
row should say: no producer AT A CHART. Same absolute is live on row
AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-glue.atlas-lft ("exactly ONE declaration") -- narrow it there too.

*** ARITHMETIC CORRECTION 2026-07-29 (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006). THE ANTECEDENT COUNT ON THIS
ROW WAS THREE-OF-THREE WHERE THE GOAL NEEDS FOUR-OF-FOUR, AND ONE SENTENCE BELOW IS MISLEADING
IN THE DIRECTION THAT MATTERS. Audited ajcr-p4's finding (I-0967/I-0977); it is CORRECT. ***

THE SENTENCE TO FIX IS MINE. Below, this row says the big-site sheaf condition, the 01JJ gluing
and "BOTH finiteness certificates -- which are DERIVED from chart-level hypotheses, not assumed"
are done and kernel-checked. Read against the statements that is wrong in effect: they are derived
from chart-level hypotheses THAT NOTHING IN THE TREE PRODUCED, which is not the same as derived.
locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom (JacobianDataCharts.lean:154) TAKES
hlft : forall i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i); it was, until 67c8d24d5, the only Picard/
declaration concluding LocallyOfFiniteType at a chart, so the certificate was an assumption on
every route. PicRepDatum.lft (PicRepDatum.lean:100) is a structure FIELD -- also an assumption --
and toJacobianData (JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum.lean:87) only carries it across. So a lane that
discharged all THREE tracked antecedents would NOT have produced a JacobianData C, which is what
Challenge.lean's frozen Jacobian := (jacobianData C).J actually needs.

NOW DISCHARGED, AND IT IS A REAL DISCHARGE RATHER THAN A RELOCATION -- the part I checked hardest,
because "reduces to X" usually just moves the bill. Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean (ajcr-p4) proves
locallyOfFiniteType_chartHom_mixedParamChart: at the REAL atlas the certificate follows from
hD : forall i, LocallyOfFiniteType (D i).hom alone. And hD is FREE at the carrier the
divisor-representability lane returns: PROBED, imports current, `lake env lean` EXIT=0 --
LocallyOfFiniteType (divSchemeOver k A B g r1 r2 b1 b2).hom closes by inferInstance ALONE at
ARBITRARY window data, via the global instance locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom
(DivSchemeQProj.lean:199), and DivOver (DivRepGlobalClassify.lean:113-116, :308) is an instance of
exactly that shape. So a lane producing rep supplies the fourth antecedent at the same moment at
zero cost.

WHAT REPLACES THE THREE-ITEM LIST, as the antecedent list of the GOAL:
 1. hf = IsChartUniv. OPEN (chart-restrict, ajcr-p1).
 2. Zariski-local surjectivity of Sigma.desc. OPEN (dat-b, ajcr-p2).
 3. rep i, divisor representability. OPEN (divrep.u2, ajcr-p3).
 4. hlft, chart finiteness. DISCHARGED at the real atlas, free at the rep carrier.
 5. quasiCompact. OPEN and GENUINELY A-POSTERIORI, and this is the item to watch now that 4 is
    gone. PER-CHART compactness is free at the same carrier (compactSpace_divScheme); CompactSpace
    of the GLUED object is not, and for the class-indexed (infinite) atlas the finite route
    JacobianData.ofCharts is unavailable, so it must come from the Abel image
    (JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage). Do not let the freeness of the per-chart form be quoted
    for the glued form -- that conflation is exactly what this correction is about.

THE VERDICT IS UNCHANGED: none of the three OPEN antecedents closes this week (I-0873). Item 4
was never on the list, so removing it does not shorten the critical path; what it does is make
the remaining list the true one. One caveat on the discharging file itself:
Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean:65 claims "everything in it other than hf, the local-surjectivity
instance and rep is now discharged", while hcpt is an explicit hypothesis of the same definition
and the file's own :184-186 and :262-265 call it open. The :262 reading is the correct one.

*** SELF-CORRECTION 2026-07-29, SAME SESSION (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0004, after a fresh-context
review of my own work). THE IsPlusHonest FINDING BELOW IS OVERSTATED ON THE STEP THAT CARRIES IT.
The route-decision conclusion SURVIVES, for a different and better-evidenced reason. ***

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I argued: relPicToPicEt lands in PicEtAff.unit, unit is mk at the TRIVIAL cover
`.self A` alone, therefore honesty asserts that no nontrivial etale cover is needed. That step is
FALSE. PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk (Picard/RelPicCoverInjective.lean:48) proves a unit class is presented on
EVERY cover E, not only on `.self` -- so "mk at the trivial cover" describes one PRESENTATION, not
the RANGE, and nothing follows about which classes the range contains.

AND THE ABSOLUTE FORM IS REFUTED BY A LANDED THEOREM IN THIS TREE:
PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section (Picard/EffectivityClose.lean:141) proves the unit SURJECTIVE
over a field test K admitting a curve point sigma, upgraded to a MulEquiv by
PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section (:186). Over such tests honesty is DISCHARGED OUTRIGHT -- vacuously
true, no etale cover needed anywhere. So "IsPlusHonest is the sheafification gap asserted of an
arbitrary section" is wrong as an absolute.

THE CORRECTED CLAIM, which is narrower and better supported. The gap is at a GENERAL AFFINE BASE
WITH NO SECTION, and the tree documents exactly why:
 * the field route closes only through etale-cover cofinality in finite separable field extensions
   (Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom, EtaleCover.lean:287) -- there is NO
   general-base analogue of that cofinality;
 * EffectivityMoving.lean:41-48 states plainly that for a merely quasi-finite (non-finite) etale
   cover the moving statement is FALSE, with a counterexample sketch (B = A_u x A_v over a
   2-dimensional normal local A with nontrivial local class group). So the [Module.Finite A B]
   hypothesis in the effectivity layer is load-bearing, not convenience.

SO THE OBSTRUCTION IS BASE-SHAPE, NOT ARBITRARINESS OF THE CLASS. Two consequences:
 1. the split to hand a prover lane is NOT "chart value (cheap) vs arbitrary section (blocked)" but
    "field test with a section (FREE) vs general sectionless affine base (OPEN)". The delta between
    the chart side and the coverage side is NARROWER than I priced it;
 2. antecedent 2 still owes a route decision -- which site coverage is local for -- because the
    repair still refines covers and descends, and Zariski-local surjectivity still will not absorb
    that. The conclusion stands; cite the module-finiteness counterexample, NOT the trivial-cover
    claim, when repeating it.

Also corrected, same review: I called DivisorFamilyAffThetaTyping.lean UNROOTED. It is ROOTED --
AlgebraicJacobian.lean:346 imports it at HEAD (commit 2b8cef366) and its .olean exists, so it IS
kernel-checked. Another lane rooted it while I was auditing it and I did not re-run the grep before
publishing. I-0941's step (i) is therefore already done; its step (ii) stands.

--- the original finding follows; read its trivial-cover reasoning as retracted ---

*** RANKING AMENDMENT, second reviewer pass 2026-07-29 (run 0082 session 0004, review-ajcr).
ANTECEDENT 2 IS NOT A GEOMETRY BILL, IT IS A SITE DECISION -- so the #2 slot below is
MIS-JUSTIFIED even though its position may be right. Issue I-0920. ***

The costing below is otherwise intact and should be read as it stands. This amendment changes ONE
thing: the reason antecedent 2 (dat-b B-5/B-6, local surjectivity) is expensive.

BELOW IT SAYS: "It carries the content, and its packaging is complete ... What it owes is geometry:
the per-point datum, plus the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation."

MEASURED, tracing the per-point datum through its own producer chain rather than through the rows'

  IF: pick c in P^1(k) outside that image and any c' /= c; then Spec R minus W_c confines D to the

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Measure build reachability: which AlgebraicJacobian modules are NOT in the
transitive import cone of the default target `AlgebraicJacobian.lean`?

A module outside the cone is never elaborated by a bare `lake build`, so any
axiom/sorry probe run against the root target silently skips it.

Usage: python3 scripts/reach.py [--json] [--counts]
Run from the project root (the directory holding AlgebraicJacobian.lean).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
LIB = ROOT / "AlgebraicJacobian"
ROOT_MODULE = "AlgebraicJacobian"

IMPORT_RE = re.compile(r"^import\s+([A-Za-z_][\w.«»]*)", re.MULTILINE)


def module_of(path: Path) -> str:
    rel = path.relative_to(ROOT).with_suffix("")
    return ".".join(rel.parts)


def imports_of(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    # imports only occur in the header, before any command
    head = text.split("\nnamespace ", 1)[0]
    return IMPORT_RE.findall(head)


def main() -> int:
    files = {module_of(p): p for p in sorted(LIB.rglob("*.lean"))}
    root_file = ROOT / f"{ROOT_MODULE}.lean"
    files[ROOT_MODULE] = root_file

    graph = {m: imports_of(p) for m, p in files.items()}

    seen: set[str] = set()
    stack = [ROOT_MODULE]
    while stack:
        m = stack.pop()
        if m in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(m)
        for dep in graph.get(m, []):
            if dep in files and dep not in seen:
                stack.append(dep)

    unrooted = sorted(m for m in files if m != ROOT_MODULE and m not in seen)
    total = len(files) - 1

    # who imports an unrooted module (from anywhere, rooted or not)?
    importers: dict[str, list[str]] = {m: [] for m in unrooted}
    for m, deps in graph.items():
        for d in deps:
            if d in importers:
                importers[d].append(m)

    if "--json" in sys.argv:
        json.dump(
            {
                "total": total,
                "rooted": total - len(unrooted),
                "unrooted": len(unrooted),
                "modules": [
                    {
                        "module": m,
                        "lines": len(files[m].read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()),
                        "imports_unrooted": sorted(
                            d for d in graph[m] if d in importers
                        ),
                        "importers": sorted(importers[m]),
                    }
                    for m in unrooted
                ],
            },
            sys.stdout,
            indent=1,
        )
        print()
        return 0

    print(f"{total} modules under {LIB.name}/; {len(unrooted)} UNROOTED")
    if "--counts" in sys.argv:
        return 0
    for m in unrooted:
        n = len(files[m].read_text(errors="replace").splitlines())
        pulls = sorted(d for d in graph[m] if d in importers)
        tag = f"  needs-unrooted: {', '.join(s.split('.')[-1] for s in pulls)}" if pulls else ""
        print(f"  {m}  ({n} lines){tag}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

pic-g 0096 landed the first producer of (divFunctor C pi 0).RepresentableBy D by proving Subsingleton at every test object and pairing it with another lane's trivSection. The obvious attack -- 'Subsingleton X is free when X is empty, so this is vacuous' -- FAILS here, and the reason is worth keeping because it tells you where to aim next time.

Subsingleton was the EXPENSIVE half. It consumed a real theorem (isUnit_eqn_of_isCertified_zero: rank-0 certificate + 1 in the glued equalizer forces every chart equation to be a unit) plus a genuine Zariski descent through IsLocallyCertified's Away localizations. Nonempty was the free half, imported: trivZar/trivSection, unconditional, another lane's landed work.

1. The two-line docstring 'Main declarations' census of the producer's own file named a declaration that exists nowhere in the workspace (I-1525), and it was precisely the carrier the chain does NOT cover (globally certified DivFam vs locally certified DivFamZar). A singleton-producer file has two carriers one import apart; the census is where they get conflated.
2. The producer's own 'what this does NOT do' paragraph carried an unproved absolute -- 'coverage is provably impossible at this parameter' -- inherited from the cited file and stated MORE strongly than the cited theorem, whose conclusion is about chartLocus while the assembly's hypothesis is about an arbitrary open (I-1526, I-1521). Direction of the error was against the lane's own interest, which is exactly why nobody re-read it.

THE RULE: when a lane produces a singleton, do not spend the audit on Subsingleton. Spend it on (a) which of the several nearby carriers the chain actually quotients, and (b) the self-limiting sentences, because a limit stated harsher than proved reads as audited and forecloses a route nobody has refuted."]

     8	/-!
     9	# Canonical cocycles of representability isomorphisms
    10	
    11	`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso` is defined by Yoneda uniqueness, but mathlib does
    12	not expose the two equations that descent data consume: its universal-element intertwining
    13	formula and transitivity for three independently chosen representing objects.  These generic
    14	lemmas make those equations explicit.  In particular, the transitivity theorem proves a
    15	three-face cocycle without defining the `1,3` face as a composite.
    16	-/

    18	set_option autoImplicit false
    19	
    20	universe v u u'
    21	
    22	open CategoryTheory
    23	
    24	namespace CategoryTheory.Functor.RepresentableBy
    25	
    26	/-- Transport a representation through the right adjoint of an adjunction.
    27	
    28	This is the categorical pullback step used for overlap bases: if `L ⊣ R`, then a
    29	representation of `F` by `Y` induces one of `L.op ⋙ F` by `R.obj Y`.  The statement
    30	requires only the adjunction; for schemes, `Over.mapPullbackAdj` supplies it whenever
    31	the relevant pullbacks exist, including tensor-product (non-field) bases. -/
    32	noncomputable def ofLeftAdjoint
    33	    {C : Type u} {D : Type u'} [Category.{v, u} C] [Category.{v, u'} D]
    34	    {L : C ⥤ D} {R : D ⥤ C} (adj : L ⊣ R)
    35	    {F : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y : D} (e : F.RepresentableBy Y) :
    36	    (L.op ⋙ F).RepresentableBy (R.obj Y) :=
    37	  (adj.representableBy Y).ofIso (Functor.isoWhiskerLeft L.op e.toIso)
    38	
    39	/-- The universal element of `ofLeftAdjoint` is obtained by applying the adjunction inverse. -/
    40	theorem ofLeftAdjoint_homEquiv
    41	    {C : Type u} {D : Type u'} [Category.{v, u} C] [Category.{v, u'} D]
    42	    {L : C ⥤ D} {R : D ⥤ C} (adj : L ⊣ R)
    43	    {F : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y : D} (e : F.RepresentableBy Y)
    44	    {X : C} (g : X ⟶ R.obj Y) :
    45	    (ofLeftAdjoint adj e).homEquiv g = e.homEquiv ((adj.homEquiv X Y).symm g) := by
    46	  rfl
    47	
    48	/-- Compare representations of two isomorphic presheaves.
    49	
    50	The source representation is first transported along `η`; the comparison is then the ordinary
    51	Yoneda comparison.  This is the canonical overlap isomorphism once the two pullback Picard
    52	presheaves have been identified. -/
    53	noncomputable def uniqueUpToIsoOfIso
    54	    {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
    55	    {F F' : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y Y' : C}
    56	    (e : F.RepresentableBy Y) (e' : F'.RepresentableBy Y') (η : F ≅ F') : Y ≅ Y' :=
    57	  (e.ofIso η).uniqueUpToIso e'
    58	
    59	/-- The comparison in `uniqueUpToIsoOfIso` intertwines the two universal elements. -/
    60	theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_hom
    61	    {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
    62	    {F F' : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y Y' : C}
    63	    (e : F.RepresentableBy Y) (e' : F'.RepresentableBy Y') (η : F ≅ F')
    64	    {X : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    65	    e'.homEquiv (f ≫ (uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e e' η).hom) =
    66	      η.hom.app (Opposite.op X) (e.homEquiv f) := by
    67	  change e'.homEquiv (f ≫ ((e.ofIso η).uniqueUpToIso e').hom) =
    68	    (e.ofIso η).homEquiv f
    69	  have h : ((e.ofIso η).uniqueUpToIso e').hom =
    70	      e'.homEquiv.symm ((e.ofIso η).homEquiv (𝟙 Y)) := rfl
    71	  rw [h, comp_homEquiv_symm, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
    72	  rw [← (e.ofIso η).homEquiv_comp f (𝟙 Y), Category.comp_id]
    73	
    74	/-- Three canonical comparisons satisfy the cocycle law when the presheaf isomorphisms do. -/
    75	theorem uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_trans
    76	    {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
    77	    {F₁ F₂ F₃ : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y₁ Y₂ Y₃ : C}
    78	    (e₁ : F₁.RepresentableBy Y₁) (e₂ : F₂.RepresentableBy Y₂)
    79	    (e₃ : F₃.RepresentableBy Y₃)
    80	    (η₁₂ : F₁ ≅ F₂) (η₂₃ : F₂ ≅ F₃) (η₁₃ : F₁ ≅ F₃)
    81	    (hη : η₁₃ = η₁₂ ≪≫ η₂₃) :
    82	    uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e₁ e₃ η₁₃ =
    83	      uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e₁ e₂ η₁₂ ≪≫ uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e₂ e₃ η₂₃ := by
    84	  apply Iso.ext
    85	  apply e₃.homEquiv.injective
    86	  calc
    87	    e₃.homEquiv (uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e₁ e₃ η₁₃).hom =
    88	        η₁₃.hom.app (Opposite.op Y₁) (e₁.homEquiv (𝟙 Y₁)) := by
    89	      simpa using homEquiv_uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_hom e₁ e₃ η₁₃ (𝟙 Y₁)
    90	    _ = η₂₃.hom.app (Opposite.op Y₁)
    91	        (η₁₂.hom.app (Opposite.op Y₁) (e₁.homEquiv (𝟙 Y₁))) := by
    92	      rw [hη]
    93	      rfl
    94	    _ = e₃.homEquiv ((uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e₁ e₂ η₁₂).hom ≫
    95	        (uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e₂ e₃ η₂₃).hom) := by
    96	      rw [homEquiv_uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_hom e₂ e₃ η₂₃]
    97	      rw [← Category.id_comp (uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e₁ e₂ η₁₂).hom,
    98	        homEquiv_uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_hom e₁ e₂ η₁₂]
    99	
   100	/-- Composition with the canonical representing-object isomorphism transports the universal
   101	element unchanged. -/
   102	theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
   103	    {F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y Y' : C} (e : F.RepresentableBy Y)
   104	    (e' : F.RepresentableBy Y') {X : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
   105	    e'.homEquiv (f ≫ (e.uniqueUpToIso e').hom) = e.homEquiv f := by
   106	  have h : (e.uniqueUpToIso e').hom =
   107	      e'.homEquiv.symm (e.homEquiv (𝟙 Y)) := rfl
   108	  rw [h, comp_homEquiv_symm, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
   109	  rw [← e.homEquiv_comp f (𝟙 Y), Category.comp_id]
   110	
   111	/-- The canonical isomorphisms between three representations satisfy the cocycle law.  The
   112	`1,3` comparison is the independently defined `uniqueUpToIso e₁ e₃`, not a composite alias. -/
   113	theorem uniqueUpToIso_trans {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
   114	    {F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y₁ Y₂ Y₃ : C}
   115	    (e₁ : F.RepresentableBy Y₁) (e₂ : F.RepresentableBy Y₂)
   116	    (e₃ : F.RepresentableBy Y₃) :
   117	    e₁.uniqueUpToIso e₃ = e₁.uniqueUpToIso e₂ ≪≫ e₂.uniqueUpToIso e₃ := by
   118	  apply Iso.ext
   119	  apply e₃.homEquiv.injective
   120	  calc
   121	    e₃.homEquiv (e₁.uniqueUpToIso e₃).hom = e₁.homEquiv (𝟙 Y₁) := by
   122	      simpa using homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom e₁ e₃ (𝟙 Y₁)
   123	    _ = e₂.homEquiv (e₁.uniqueUpToIso e₂).hom := by
   124	      symm
   125	      simpa using homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom e₁ e₂ (𝟙 Y₁)
   126	    _ = e₃.homEquiv
   127	        ((e₁.uniqueUpToIso e₂).hom ≫ (e₂.uniqueUpToIso e₃).hom) := by
   128	      symm
   129	      exact homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom e₂ e₃ (e₁.uniqueUpToIso e₂).hom
   130	
   131	end CategoryTheory.Functor.RepresentableBy

    10	/-!
    11	# The tensor-overlap comparison for Picard representability
    12	
    13	For a field extension `k → L`, the two coprojections
    14	`L → L ⊗[k] L` induce two pullbacks of an L-side representation.  This file
    15	constructs the comparison between those two representing schemes.  Each pullback
    16	is obtained from `Over.mapPullbackAdj`; the presheaf comparison is assembled from
    17	the landed theta isomorphism and the equality of the two composites back to `k`.
    18	
    19	The construction deliberately stops before the triple-tensor face equation.  That
    20	remaining equation is the genuine effectivity/coherence consumer of this module and
    21	must use the three tensor-face maps, rather than a definitional shortcut.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	set_option autoImplicit false
    25	
    26	universe u
    27	
    28	open CategoryTheory
    29	open scoped TensorProduct
    30	
    31	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    32	
    33	variable {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    34	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    35	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    36	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    37	
    38	/-! ## The two tensor coprojections and their common base map -/
    39	
    40	/-- The first map `Spec (L ⊗[k] L) ⟶ Spec L`. -/
    41	noncomputable def tensorOverlapInl :
    42	    Spec (.of (L ⊗[k] L)) ⟶ Spec (.of L) :=
    43	  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    44	    (tensorInl (k := k) (A := k) (B := L)).toRingHom)
    45	
    46	/-- The second map `Spec (L ⊗[k] L) ⟶ Spec L`. -/
    47	noncomputable def tensorOverlapInr :
    48	    Spec (.of (L ⊗[k] L)) ⟶ Spec (.of L) :=
    49	  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    50	    (tensorInr (k := k) (A := k) (B := L)).toRingHom)
    51	
    52	/-- The common map to `Spec k` obtained from either tensor coprojection. -/
    53	noncomputable def tensorOverlapBase :
    54	    Spec (.of L) ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
    55	  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))
    56	
    57	/-- The two tensor coprojections have the same composite to the challenge base. -/
    58	lemma tensorOverlapInl_comp_base :
    59	    tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L) ≫ tensorOverlapBase (k := k) (L := L) =
    60	      tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L) ≫ tensorOverlapBase (k := k) (L := L) := by
    61	  simp only [tensorOverlapInl, tensorOverlapInr, tensorOverlapBase]
    62	  rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← Spec.map_comp]
    63	  have h := tensorInl_comp_ofId (k := k) (A := k) (B := L)
    64	  congr 1
    65	  ext x
    66	  exact DFunLike.congr_fun h x
    67	
    68	/-! ## The presheaf comparison -/
    69	
    70	/-- Rebase an L-side Picard functor along one tensor coprojection, then identify it
    71	with the fixed k-side functor through theta and the common composite to `Spec k`. -/
    72	noncomputable def tensorOverlapCommon
    73	    (f : Spec (.of (L ⊗[k] L)) ⟶ Spec (.of L)) :
    74	    (Over.map f).op ⋙ pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C) ≅
    75	      (Over.map (f ≫ tensorOverlapBase (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
    76	        pic0TypeFunctor C :=
    77	  Functor.isoWhiskerLeft (Over.map f).op (pic0ThetaType k L C) ≪≫
    78	    (Functor.associator (Over.map f).op (Over.map (tensorOverlapBase (k := k) (L := L))).op
    79	      (pic0TypeFunctor C)).symm ≪≫
    80	    (Functor.isoWhiskerRight
    81	      (NatIso.op (Over.mapComp f (tensorOverlapBase (k := k) (L := L))))
    82	      (pic0TypeFunctor C)).symm
    83	
    84	/-- The canonical natural isomorphism between the two tensor-coprojection pullback
    85	presheaves. -/
    86	noncomputable def tensorOverlapTheta :
    87	    (Over.map (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
    88	        pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C) ≅
    89	      (Over.map (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
    90	        pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C) :=
    91	  tensorOverlapCommon (C := C) (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L)) ≪≫
    92	    eqToIso (congrArg
    93	      (fun g => (Over.map g).op ⋙ pic0TypeFunctor C)
    94	      (tensorOverlapInl_comp_base (k := k) (L := L))) ≪≫
    95	    (tensorOverlapCommon (C := C) (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))).symm
    96	
    97	/-! ## Pullback representations and the canonical scheme isomorphism -/
    98	
    99	variable {J : Over (Spec (.of L))}
   100	
   101	/-- The representation pulled back along the first tensor coprojection. -/
   102	noncomputable def tensorOverlapRepInl
   103	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).RepresentableBy J) :
   104	    ((Over.map (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
   105	      pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).RepresentableBy
   106	        ((Over.pullback (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))).obj J) :=
   107	  Functor.RepresentableBy.ofLeftAdjoint
   108	    (Over.mapPullbackAdj (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))) rep
   109	
   110	/-- The representation pulled back along the second tensor coprojection. -/
   111	noncomputable def tensorOverlapRepInr
   112	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).RepresentableBy J) :
   113	    ((Over.map (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
   114	      pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).RepresentableBy
   115	        ((Over.pullback (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))).obj J) :=
   116	  Functor.RepresentableBy.ofLeftAdjoint
   117	    (Over.mapPullbackAdj (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))) rep
   118	
   119	/-- The canonical representing-scheme isomorphism on the double tensor overlap. -/
   120	noncomputable def tensorOverlapIso
   121	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).RepresentableBy J) :
   122	    (Over.pullback (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))).obj J ≅
   123	      (Over.pullback (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))).obj J :=
   124	  Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIsoOfIso
   125	    (tensorOverlapRepInl rep) (tensorOverlapRepInr rep)
   126	    (tensorOverlapTheta (C := C))
   127	
   128	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
   129	-- The expanded Over pullback comparison crosses several categorical
   130	-- functors; its definitional check exceeds Lean's default heartbeat budget.
   131	/-- Universal-element characterization of the tensor-overlap comparison. -/
   132	theorem tensorOverlapIso_homEquiv
   133	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).RepresentableBy J)
   134	    {T : Over (Spec (.of (L ⊗[k] L)))}
   135	    (f : T ⟶ (Over.pullback (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))).obj J) :
   136	    (tensorOverlapRepInr rep).homEquiv
   137	        (f ≫ (tensorOverlapIso rep).hom) =
   138	      (tensorOverlapTheta (C := C)).hom.app (Opposite.op T)
   139	        ((tensorOverlapRepInl rep).homEquiv f) :=
   140	  Functor.RepresentableBy.homEquiv_uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_hom
   141	    (tensorOverlapRepInl rep) (tensorOverlapRepInr rep)
   142	    (tensorOverlapTheta (C := C)) f
   143	
   144	end AlgebraicGeometry

BASE="$BASE" SNAP="$SNAP" CENSUS_TMP="$tmp" python3 - <<'"'PY'
import os
from pathlib import Path
from collections import Counter
from archon_horizon.search.index import extract_declarations

tmp = Path(os.environ[\"CENSUS_TMP\"])
projects = {
    \"AJC\": \"MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge\",
    \"AJCR\": \"MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild\",
}

def split_sig(sig):
    par = bra = cur = 0
    for i, ch in enumerate(sig):
        if ch == \"(\":
            par += 1
        elif ch == \")\":
            par = max(0, par - 1)
        elif ch == \"[\":
            bra += 1
        elif ch == \"]\":
            bra = max(0, bra - 1)
        elif ch == \"{\":
            cur += 1
        elif ch == \"}\":
            cur = max(0, cur - 1)
        elif ch == \":\" and par == bra == cur == 0:
            return sig[:i], sig[i+1:]
    return sig, \"\"

def census(root, rel):
    base = root / rel
    files = sorted(base.rglob(\"*.lean\"))
    decls = []
    raw = 0
    for p in files:
        text = p.read_text()
        raw += text.count(\"(rep :\")
        decls.extend(extract_declarations(text, library=rel, file=str(p.relative_to(root))))
    strict_occ = sum(d.signature.count(\"(rep :\") for d in decls)
    strict_decls = sum(\"(rep :\" in d.signature for d in decls)
    rows = []
    for d in decls:
        pre, res = split_sig(d.signature)
        ic = pre.count(\".RepresentableBy\")
        rc = res.count(\".RepresentableBy\")
        rows.append((d.file, d.name, ic, rc, d.signature))
    return {
        \"files\": len(files), \"decls\": len(decls), \"raw\": raw,
        \"strict_occ\": strict_occ, \"strict_decls\": strict_decls,
        \"input_occ\": sum(r[2] for r in rows),
        \"input_decls\": sum(r[2] > 0 for r in rows),
        \"result_occ\": sum(r[3] for r in rows),
        \"result_decls\": sum(r[3] > 0 for r in rows),
        \"direct\": sum(r[3] > 0 and r[2] == 0 for r in rows),
        \"rows\": rows,
    }

print(\"BASE\", os.environ[\"BASE\"])
print(\"SNAP\", os.environ[\"SNAP\"])
for name, rel in projects.items():
    b = census(tmp / \"base\", rel)
    h = census(tmp / \"head\", rel)
    keys = [\"files\",\"decls\",\"raw\",\"strict_occ\",\"strict_decls\",\"input_occ\",\"input_decls\",\"result_occ\",\"result_decls\",\"direct\"]
    print(name)
    for k in keys:
        print(f\"  {k}: {b[k]} -> {h[k]} (delta {h[k]-b[k]:+d})\")
    bkeys = {(r[0],r[1]) for r in b[\"rows\"]}
    print(\"  new relevant declarations:\")
    for f,n,ic,rc,sig in h[\"rows\"]:
        if (f,n) not in bkeys and (ic or rc):
            print(f\"    {f}:{n}: input={ic} result={rc}\")
PY
rm -rf \""'$tmp"'"}, "usage": null}

    10	/-!
    11	# A presheaf with unique values is represented by the terminal object
    12	
    13	This file supplies the categorical bridge that was missing between "a presheaf
    14	`F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v` has exactly one element at every test object" and
    15	"`F` is representable by the terminal object of `C`".
    16	
    17	Mathlib `v4.31` has `CategoryTheory.Limits.hasTerminal_of_unique` (a `C`-object
    18	`X` with `Unique (Y ⟶ X)` for every `Y` is terminal) and
    19	`CategoryTheory.Limits.IsTerminal.ofUnique`, but **not** the presheaf-side
    20	statement: from `Nonempty (F.obj T)` and `Subsingleton (F.obj T)` at every `T`,
    21	build the natural bijection `(X ⟶ Y) ≃ F.obj (op X)` that
    22	`Functor.RepresentableBy` is. Both sides of that bijection are singletons —
    23	the left because `Y` is terminal, the right by hypothesis — so the bijection
    24	and its naturality are `Subsingleton.elim`. Verified absent by search over
    25	mathlib and both projects; the nearest hits (`hasTerminal_of_unique`,
    26	`isTerminalEquivUnique`) are about representing objects, not represented
    27	presheaves.
    28	
    29	## Why it is worth a named declaration
    30	
    31	`Functor.RepresentableBy` is *data* (a chosen `Equiv` per object, plus a
    32	naturality equation), not a `Prop`. So even when a presheaf is manifestly a
    33	subterminal-and-inhabited functor, producing the `RepresentableBy` witness
    34	still requires building that `Equiv` by hand at every use site. This file does
    35	it once, at full categorical generality, so a consumer that has proved
    36	`Nonempty` and `Subsingleton` pointwise gets the representability witness by a
    37	single application — no `Equiv` plumbing.
    38	
    39	## The intended consumer
    40	
    41	`Picard/DivFamilyZero.lean` proves `Nonempty ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T))`
    42	for every `π` and test `T` (`DivFunctorDeg.instNonemptyObjZero`, the empty
    43	divisor). If a lane proves the matching
    44	`Subsingleton ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T))` — that the empty divisor is the
    45	*only* relative effective divisor of degree `0` — then
    46	`representableByTerminal` yields
    47	`(DivFunctorDeg π 0).RepresentableBy (Over.mk (𝟙 S))` immediately, the first
    48	genuine `RepresentableBy` producer on the AJC divisor side. That `Subsingleton`
    49	is real content (a fact about `fiberDeg`, a `finrank` with a junk value at
    50	infinite dimension), and it is **not** discharged here; this file supplies only
    51	the categorical interface it plugs into.
    52	
    53	Everything here is about an arbitrary category and carries no algebraic-geometry
    54	hypothesis; nothing closes any `sorry`.
    55	-/
    56	
    57	universe w v u
    58	
    59	namespace CategoryTheory.Functor
    60	
    61	variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    62	
    63	/-- **A presheaf that is pointwise nonempty and subsingleton is represented by
    64	any terminal object.**
    65	
    66	The representing map `(X ⟶ Y) ≃ F.obj (op X)` sends every morphism to the
    67	unique element of `F.obj (op X)` and back to the unique morphism `X ⟶ Y` (which
    68	exists because `Y` is terminal). Both round trips, and the naturality square,
    69	are forced by the two `Subsingleton`s.
    70	
    71	This is the presheaf-side companion of `Limits.hasTerminal_of_unique`, which is
    72	absent from mathlib `v4.31`. -/
    73	noncomputable def representableByTerminal (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) {Y : C}
    74	    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y)
    75	    (hne : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Nonempty (F.obj T)) (hss : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Subsingleton (F.obj T)) :
    76	    F.RepresentableBy Y where
    77	  homEquiv {X} := by
    78	    haveI := hne (Opposite.op X)
    79	    haveI := hss (Opposite.op X)
    80	    exact
    81	      { toFun := fun _ => Classical.arbitrary _
    82	        invFun := fun _ => hY.from X
    83	        left_inv := fun _ => hY.hom_ext _ _
    84	        right_inv := fun _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _ }
    85	  homEquiv_comp {X X'} f g := by
    86	    haveI := hss (Opposite.op X)
    87	    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
    88	
    89	/-- **The `Unique`-packaged form of `representableByTerminal`.** When the values
    90	of `F` are literally `Unique` (a single default plus subsingleton), the same
    91	terminal object represents it. -/
    92	noncomputable def representableByTerminal_of_unique (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) {Y : C}
    93	    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y) (h : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Unique (F.obj T)) :
    94	    F.RepresentableBy Y :=
    95	  representableByTerminal F hY (fun T => ⟨(h T).default⟩) (fun T => (h T).instSubsingleton)
    96	
    97	/-- **Existence corollary**: a pointwise nonempty-and-subsingleton presheaf is
    98	representable (forgets the chosen terminal object). -/
    99	theorem isRepresentable_of_terminal (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) {Y : C}
   100	    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y)
   101	    (hne : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Nonempty (F.obj T)) (hss : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Subsingleton (F.obj T)) :
   102	    F.IsRepresentable :=
   103	  (representableByTerminal F hY hne hss).isRepresentable
   104

     9	/-!
    10	# The empty divisor: the first inhabitant of `Scheme.DivFamily`
    11	
    12	`Scheme.DivFamily π T` (`Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean`) is the carrier of the whole
    13	divisor side of the Milne–Kollár campaign: `Scheme.DivFunctor`, its degree slices
    14	`Scheme.DivFunctorDeg`, the Abel maps `abelDeg` / `abelMapWitness`, the flatness
    15	inputs of `Picard/DivPushforwardFlat.lean`, and `IdentityComponent`'s
    16	`ClassDegreePinned` acceptance test are all quantified over it. Until this file it
    17	had **zero producers**, for any `π`, any base, and any test object including the
    18	trivial one — measured with `exact?` and recorded in its own docstring. The
    19	consequence recorded there: *every* statement quantified over a `DivFamily` was
    20	"true but untested", with no instance to be wrong about.
    21	
    22	This file supplies the first inhabitant, unconditionally in `π : X ⟶ S` and
    23	`T : Over S`: the **empty divisor** `D = ∅`, whose structure sheaf `O_D` is the
    24	zero module and whose ideal is all of `O_{X_T}`.
    25	
    26	## Why the empty divisor satisfies the divisor condition
    27	
    28	The divisor condition of `DivFamily` is that the kernel ideal `I = ker q` be
    29	*invertible* (`LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial`). For `q : O_{X_T} ⟶ 0` the kernel is
    30	`O_{X_T}` itself (`Limits.kernelZeroIsoSource`), and the structure sheaf is
    31	trivially locally trivial (`Scheme.PicSharp.isLocallyTrivial_unit`, restated here as
    32	`isLocallyTrivial_unit'` because that one is `private`). So the invertible-ideal
    33	condition — the field that makes `DivFamily` a divisor rather than an arbitrary
    34	quotient — holds *for the reason it should*: `O_{X_T}/O_{X_T} = 0` cuts out the
    35	empty subscheme, an effective divisor of degree zero.
    36	
    37	The three remaining fields are properties of the zero module, and the file proves
    38	each rather than assuming it:
    39	
    40	* `isFinitePresentation` — the zero module is finitely presented. Mathlib has no
    41	  instance for this (measured: `infer_instance` and `exact?` both fail on
    42	  `(0 : Y.Modules).IsFinitePresentation`), so §1 builds the `QuasicoherentData`:
    43	  the singleton family `{⊤}` covers the top of the opens site
    44	  (`coversTop_singleton_top`), the restriction functor preserves zero objects
    45	  (`preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor`, proved from `PresheafOfModules` extensionality
    46	  because instance search for it times out), and a zero sheaf of modules has an
    47	  *empty* presentation — no generators and no relations, both trivially finite.
    48	* `flat` — flatness over the base. The section modules of a zero module are
    49	  subsingletons, and a subsingleton module is flat.
    50	* `properSupport` — the schematic support of the zero module is the subscheme cut
    51	  out by the annihilator, which is `⊤`, so the support is **empty**
    52	  (`Scheme.IdealSheafData.instIsEmptyCarrierCarrierCommRingCatSubschemeTop`) and any
    53	  morphism out of it is proper via `IsProper.instOfIsFinite`. It is free here for that
    54	  reason, and in particular with **no properness assumption on `π`**. (An earlier
    55	  revision added "and it is a real hypothesis for a nonempty divisor". That half was
    56	  never measured — nothing here or elsewhere in the project exhibits a divisor where
    57	  `properSupport` fails or is expensive, and `DivFunctorDef.lean` says it is *automatic*
    58	  when `π` is proper. Dropped rather than repaired: the free-here half is what this
    59	  file establishes.)
    60	
    61	## What this does and does not buy
    62	
    63	**Does**: the divisor cluster is no longer vacuous. `Nonempty (DivFamily π T)` for
    64	every `π` and `T`; `(DivFunctor π).obj (op T)` and `(DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T)`
    65	are inhabited; `HasFiberDeg zero 0`; and the base-change action carries `zero` to
    66	`zero` (`pullbackAlong_zero`), so the classes are a global section of `DivFunctor`
    67	rather than a fibrewise accident. Every theorem in `DivDegree.lean` and
    68	`DivPushforwardFlat.lean` now has a witness to be checked against.
    69	
    70	**Does not**: this closes no `sorry` and witnesses no antecedent of
    71	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`. In particular it is *not* a step of D1′: the
    72	campaign's D1′ wants divisor families of a **prescribed positive degree** `d`
    73	arising from a very ample `O(1)`, which needs the projectivity input
    74	(`AJC.picrep.projectivity`) and P5 uniform `H¹` vanishing. What the empty divisor
    75	does for that programme is remove the possibility that the target type is
    76	uninhabited — a question that had to be settled before any positive-degree producer
    77	could be believed, and which no lane had settled in either direction.
    78	
    79	**One caveat, stated because it is the natural over-reading.** The degree-zero slice
    80	being inhabited does *not* make `DivFunctorDeg π 0` representable by the terminal
    81	object `Over.mk (𝟙 S)`. That would need the slice to be a *singleton* at every test
    82	object, and this file proves only the `Nonempty` half. The missing half is

Capture BASE once, before read-tree, and reuse that literal.

Damage was nil (both edits whitespace-only; I normalized the YAML across all three shas and the content is identical, and the owning lane then re-landed their wrapping as 73e93c577c). The lesson is the idiom, not the outcome.

   937	  morphism classifying a class \emph{is} the classifying morphism of that class; hence
   938	  \(\gamma_S(\rho_S(v)) = v\).
   939	
   940	  \(\rho_S \circ \gamma_S = \id\): given \(D\), both \(\rho_S(\gamma_S(D))\) and \(D\) are
   941	  classified by the single morphism \(\gamma_S(D)\) --- the first by the hypothesis on
   942	  \(\rho\), the second by the characterizing property of \(\gamma_S\)
   943	  (\ref{thm:divClassifyZar}). By separation (\ref{thm:eq_of_isDivRepClassify}) two classes
   944	  classified by the same morphism are equal, so \(\rho_S(\gamma_S(D)) = D\). (In particular
   945	  this round-trip law need not be assumed in \ref{def:divRepAffinePullback}: it is a
   946	  consequence of the clause law and separation.)
   947	
   948	  Naturality of the bijection in \(S\) is the naturality assumed of \(\rho\).
   949	\end{proof}
   950	
   951	\begin{theorem}[The universal certified family --- unproved]
   952	  \label{thm:divRepUniversalFamily}
   953	  \uses{def:divRepAffinePullback, def:divScheme, def:certifiedDivisorFamily,
   954	    thm:divisorWindow_eq_of_le, thm:isCertified_chart_obstruction}
   955	  \notready
   956	  There exists an affine pullback package for \(\mathbf{Div}\) in the sense of
   957	  \ref{def:divRepAffinePullback}; equivalently, there is a compatible chart family --- a
   958	  certified divisor family \(U_{ij}\) of degree \(g\) over the coordinate ring of each
   959	  affine chart of \(\mathbf{Div}\), whose window pair is the tautological pair of that
   960	  chart, and whose pullbacks along two presentations of one morphism agree in
   961	  \(\Div^{\,g}_{\mathrm{Zar}}\).
   962	
   963	  This statement is not proved. It is the forward direction of representability: given a
   964	  point \((K_1, K_2)\) of \(\mathbf{Div}\) over \(R\), one must produce the divisor whose
   965	  windows are \(K_1\) and \(K_2\). The intended construction takes a generating family of
   966	  \(K_1\) inside \(R \otimes_k H_M\) and reads its common vanishing locus as an effective
   967	  divisor, with local equations extracted chart by chart; the two obstacles are that this
   968	  produces the local equations only after a Zariski localisation of \(R\) --- which is why
   969	  the target is \(\Div^{\,g}_{\mathrm{Zar}}\) and not \(\Div^{\,g}\), and why the global
   970	  certificate of \ref{def:isCertified} is unavailable
   971	  (\ref{thm:isCertified_chart_obstruction}) --- and that the resulting family's second
   972	  window must be shown to be exactly \(K_2\), for which the containment
   973	  \(K_2 \subseteq K_{M+s}\) has to be upgraded from the fibrewise statement to a relative
   974	  one, an upgrade that fails over nonreduced base rings if attempted fibrewise.
   975	
   976	  Everything in Sections~\ref{sec:divfam}--\ref{sec:divclassify} is independent of this
   977	  statement.
   978	\end{theorem}

   980	\begin{corollary}[From the divisor scheme to the Jacobian]
   981	  \label{cor:divRepToJacobian}
   982	  \uses{thm:divRepAffinePullback_equiv, thm:divRepUniversalFamily,
   983	    def:pic0RepresentableByOfCharts, def:jacobian_data, def:divFamZar,
   984	    def:localEquations_picClass}

     9	# The Abel-source interface: properness and irreducibility of the Jacobian
    10	(Wave-5 D3, routes P-B / GI-(a))
    11	
    12	`AbelSourceData d` packages a proper, geometrically irreducible source scheme `D` over
    13	`k` together with an *Abel morphism* `abel : D ⟶ d.J` into the representing object of
    14	the Jacobian datum whose underlying scheme map is surjective.  Two of the three frozen
    15	Wave-5 targets are theorems **conditional on this interface** (w5-worksheet §1 D3):
    16	
    17	* `universallyClosed_of_abelSource` (**P2**): `UniversallyClosed d.J.hom` — `d.J` is
    18	  the image of the proper source: `abel.left ≫ d.J.hom = D.hom` (`Over.w`) is
    19	  universally closed and `abel.left` is surjective, so mathlib's
    20	  `UniversallyClosed.of_comp_surjective` applies.
    21	* `isProper_of_abelSource` (**P3**): `IsProper d.J.hom` — assembly of X1
    22	  separatedness (`JacobianData.isSeparated`), P2, and the datum's
    23	  `locallyOfFiniteType` certificate (quasi-compactness is implied, `UC → QC`).
    24	* `geometricallyIrreducible_of_abelSource` (**G1**, route GI-(a)): for every field
    25	  `K/k` the base change `D_K` is irreducible (the certificate), the base-changed Abel
    26	  morphism `D_K ⟶ J_K` is surjective (`Surjective` is stable under base change), and
    27	  a continuous surjective image of an irreducible space is irreducible
    28	  (`Function.Surjective.irreducibleSpace`) — so `J_K` is irreducible, uniformly in
    29	  `K`, which is exactly the `geometrically` quantifier.
    30	
    31	## Design decisions recorded (the interface spelling)
    32	
    33	* **Geometric-irreducibility certificate.**  `GeometricallyIrreducible D.hom` alone:
    34	  G1 consumes exactly per-`K` irreducibility of `D_K`, and neither P2 nor P3 consumes
    35	  reducedness — so no `GeometricallyReduced`/`GeometricallyIntegral` field is carried.
    36	  (The eventual producer has integrality available anyway and mathlib's
    37	  `GeometricallyIntegral → GeometricallyIrreducible` instance bridges,
    38	  `Geometrically/Integral.lean`.)
    39	* **Surjectivity certificate.**  The single field `Surjective abel.left` (mathlib's
    40	  topological surjectivity class) suffices for BOTH consumers.  Probe result: the
    41	  pinned mathlib has `MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange @Surjective`
    42	  (`AlgebraicGeometry/PullbackCarrier.lean:431`), so surjectivity base-changes to
    43	  every field `K/k` — no `∀ K`-quantified field is needed.
    44	* **Topology bridge.**  The "continuous surjective image of an irreducible space is
    45	  irreducible" brick anticipated by the recon (§3.3) already exists in the pinned
    46	  mathlib: `Function.Surjective.irreducibleSpace` (`Topology/Irreducible.lean:540`).
    47	  No project-side topology infrastructure is required.
    48	
    49	## The P1 discharge route (recorded for the GATED producer; do NOT build here)
    50	
    51	No instance of `AbelSourceData` is constructed in this file — the producer (brick P1)
    52	is gated on the DD lanes' shapes freezing (w5-worksheet §1 D3).  Its recorded route:
    53	
    54	* `D` := the proper degree-`n` divisor scheme (`Div^n`, `n ≥ genus C`) from the
    55	  DD-Q/DD-R quasi-projectivity campaign; `isProper` from that construction;
    56	  `geometricallyIrreducible` from geometric integrality of `C^n_K` (iterated

    62	  degree shifter (`RiemannRoch/FiberTwist.lean:301`, `classDeg_fiberTwist :393` — no
    63	  rational point needed).
    64	* `surjective` := field-point coverage from `riemann_inequality_curve`
    65	  (`RiemannRoch/ChiCurve.lean:183`): for every point of `d.J.left`, its residue-field

    99	  /-- The Abel morphism, over `Spec k`. -/
   100	  abel : D ⟶ d.J

   109	of the representing object of a Jacobian datum is universally closed, given any Abel
   110	source.  Milne's completeness step: `abel.left ≫ d.J.hom = a.D.hom` (`Over.w`) is
   111	universally closed since `a.D` is proper, and `abel.left` is surjective, so
   112	`UniversallyClosed.of_comp_surjective` applies. -/
   113	theorem universallyClosed_of_abelSource (a : AbelSourceData d) :
   114	    UniversallyClosed d.J.hom := by
   115	  haveI : UniversallyClosed (a.abel.left ≫ d.J.hom) := by
   116	    rw [Over.w a.abel]
   117	    exact a.isProper.toUniversallyClosed
   118	  haveI : Surjective a.abel.left := a.surjective
   119	  exact UniversallyClosed.of_comp_surjective a.abel.left d.J.hom

   127	  haveI : IsSeparated d.J.hom := d.isSeparated
   128	  haveI : UniversallyClosed d.J.hom := universallyClosed_of_abelSource a
   129	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType d.J.hom := d.locallyOfFiniteType
   130	  ⟨⟩

   139	theorem geometricallyIrreducible_of_abelSource (a : AbelSourceData d) :

widen=re.compile(r'\b(DivFamZarAff|divFamZarAff|divFunctorAff|IsLocallyCertifiedAff|AffAdaptation)\b')
pic=re.compile(r'(PicEtAff|picEt|relPic|pic0|Pic0|abelDiv|chartValue|picEtAff|CechPic|picClass|relPicMk|unit)')
hits=[]
for f in files:
    txt=subprocess.run(["git","--git-dir",GD,"--work-tree",".","show",rev+":"+f],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout
    lines=txt.split("\n")
    # split into declarations
    idxs=[i for i,l in enumerate(lines) if declre.match(l)]
    for a,i in enumerate(idxs):
        j=idxs[a+1] if a+1<len(idxs) else len(lines)
        body="\n".join(lines[i:j])
        # statement = up to first ':=' at depth or 'by' or 'where'
        m=re.search(r':=|\bby\b|\bwhere\b', body)
        stmt=body[:m.start()] if m else body
        if widen.search(stmt) and pic.search(stmt):
            name=lines[i].strip()[:150]
            hits.append((f.replace(P+"/AlgebraicJacobian/",""), i+1, name))
for h in hits: print(f"{h[0]}:{h[1]}  {h[2]}")
print("TOTAL", len(hits))

from pathlib import Path
import re, sys
from archon_horizon.search.index import extract_declarations

tmp = Path(sys.argv[1])
head_sha = sys.argv[2]
projects = {
    \"AJC\": \"MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/AlgebraicJacobian\",
    \"AJCR\": \"MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian\",
}

def split_result(signature: str):
    depth = 0
    in_string = False
    esc = False
    for i, ch in enumerate(signature):
        if in_string:
            if esc:
                esc = False
            elif ch == \"\\\\\":
                esc = True
            elif ch == '\"':
                in_string = False
            continue
        if ch == '\"':
            in_string = True
        elif ch in \"([{\":
            depth += 1
        elif ch in \")]}\":
            depth = max(0, depth - 1)
        elif ch == \":\" and depth == 0:
            return signature[:i], signature[i+1:]
    return signature, \"\"

def census(root: Path, rel: str):
    files = sorted((root / rel).rglob(\"*.lean\"))
    raw = strict_occ = strict_decls = 0
    input_occ = input_decls = result_occ = result_decls = direct = 0
    direct_rows = []
    consumer_rows = []
    result_rows = []
    for path in files:
        text = path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")
        raw += text.count(\"(rep :\")
        decls = extract_declarations(text, library=rel, file=str(path.relative_to(root)))
        for d in decls:
            sig = d.signature
            nstrict = sig.count(\"(rep :\")
            strict_occ += nstrict
            strict_decls += bool(nstrict)
            prefix, result = split_result(sig)
            ni = prefix.count(\".RepresentableBy\")
            nr = result.count(\".RepresentableBy\")
            input_occ += ni
            input_decls += bool(ni)
            result_occ += nr
            result_decls += bool(nr)
            if nr and not ni:
                direct += 1
                direct_rows.append((d.name, d.file, d.line))
            if ni:
                consumer_rows.append((d.name, d.file, d.line, ni, nr))
            if nr:
                result_rows.append((d.name, d.file, d.line, ni, nr))
    return {
        \"files\": len(files), \"raw\": raw,
        \"strict_occ\": strict_occ, \"strict_decls\": strict_decls,
        \"input_occ\": input_occ, \"input_decls\": input_decls,
        \"result_occ\": result_occ, \"result_decls\": result_decls,
        \"direct\": direct,
        \"direct_rows\": direct_rows, \"consumer_rows\": consumer_rows,
        \"result_rows\": result_rows,
    }

print(f\"HEAD {head_sha}\")
for label, rel in projects.items():
    b = census(tmp / \"base\", rel)
    h = census(tmp / \"head\", rel)
    print(label)
    for key in (\"files\",\"raw\",\"strict_occ\",\"strict_decls\",\"input_occ\",\"input_decls\",\"result_occ\",\"result_decls\",\"direct\"):

    bd = {x[0] for x in b[\"direct_rows\"]}

    print(\"  new_direct:\")

    print(\"  new_consumers:\")
    bc = {x[0] for x in b[\"consumer_rows\"]}
    for row in h[\"consumer_rows\"]:

    print(\"  new_results:\")
    br = {x[0] for x in b[\"result_rows\"]}
    for row in h[\"result_rows\"]:
        if row[0] not in br:
            print(\"   \", row)

from pathlib import Path

root=Path(sys.argv[1]); head=sys.argv[2]
projects={\"AJC\":\"MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/AlgebraicJacobian\",\"AJCR\":\"MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian\"}
def parts(sig):
    d=0; quote=False; esc=False
    for i,c in enumerate(sig):
        if quote:
            if esc: esc=False
            elif c==\"\\\\\": esc=True
            elif c=='\"': quote=False
        elif c=='\"': quote=True
        elif c in \"([{\": d+=1
        elif c in \")]}\": d=max(0,d-1)
        elif c==\":\" and d==0: return sig[:i],sig[i+1:]
    return sig,\"\"
def one(base,rel):
    fs=list((base/rel).rglob(\"*.lean\")); vals=[0]*9; direct=[]
    for p in fs:
        t=p.read_text(); vals[0]+=1; vals[1]+=t.count(\"(rep :\")
        for x in extract_declarations(t,library=rel,file=str(p.relative_to(base))):
            s=x.signature; vals[2]+=s.count(\"(rep :\"); vals[3]+=bool(s.count(\"(rep :\"))
            a,b=parts(s); ni=a.count(\".RepresentableBy\"); nr=b.count(\".RepresentableBy\")
            vals[4]+=ni; vals[5]+=bool(ni); vals[6]+=nr; vals[7]+=bool(nr); vals[8]+=bool(nr and not ni)
            if nr and not ni: direct.append(x.name)
    return vals,direct
print(\"HEAD\",head)
for p,rel in projects.items():
    b,bd=one(root/\"base\",rel); h,hd=one(root/\"head\",rel)
    print(p,\"files raw strictOcc strictDecls inputOcc inputDecls resultOcc resultDecls direct\")
    print(\"BASE\",*b); print(\"HEAD\",*h); print(\"DELTA\",*(y-x for x,y in zip(b,h)))
    print(\"NEW_DIRECT\",*[n for n in hd if n not in bd],sep=\"\\n\")

/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
import os, subprocess
G=os.environ['HORIZON_GIT']; base='c56d433e8a99a82babf50aecb3e6fec48410e2a2'; head=subprocess.check_output([G,'rev-parse','HEAD'],text=True).strip()
def run(*args): return subprocess.check_output([G,*args],text=True)
# commits reachable base..head, oldest first
cs=run('log','--reverse','--format=%H',f'{base}..{head}').splitlines()
for c in cs:
    fmt=run('show','-s','--format=%H%x09%s%x09%(trailers:key=Archon-Task,valueonly)%x09%(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)',c).rstrip('\\n')
    paths=run('diff-tree','--no-commit-id','--name-only','-r',c).splitlines()
    lean=[p for p in paths if p.endswith('.lean') and ('Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge' in p)]
    if lean:
      print(fmt)
      print('  '+'\\n  '.join(lean))
PY"

    affine comparison picEtAffineEquiv (via the landed picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt):

    is a conjugation of the landed unitEquiv_of_section by the affine comparison iso,

    (on PicEtAff) and the functor the rep headline names (picEt/pic0). Both key

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.EtaleSeparatedness
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ThetaCocycle
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RepresentableByCocycle

/-!
# The tensor-overlap comparison for Picard representability

For a field extension `k → L`, the two coprojections
`L → L ⊗[k] L` induce two pullbacks of an L-side representation.  This file
constructs the comparison between those two representing schemes.  Each pullback
is obtained from `Over.mapPullbackAdj`; the presheaf comparison is assembled from
the landed theta isomorphism and the equality of the two composites back to `k`.

The construction deliberately stops before the triple-tensor face equation.  That
remaining equation is the genuine effectivity/coherence consumer of this module and
must use the three tensor-face maps, rather than a definitional shortcut.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

/-! ## The two tensor coprojections and their common base map -/

/-- The first map `Spec (L ⊗[k] L) ⟶ Spec L`. -/
noncomputable def tensorOverlapInl :
    Spec (.of (L ⊗[k] L)) ⟶ Spec (.of L) :=
  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    (tensorInl (k := k) (A := k) (B := L)).toRingHom)

/-- The second map `Spec (L ⊗[k] L) ⟶ Spec L`. -/
noncomputable def tensorOverlapInr :
    Spec (.of (L ⊗[k] L)) ⟶ Spec (.of L) :=
  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    (tensorInr (k := k) (A := k) (B := L)).toRingHom)

/-- The common map to `Spec k` obtained from either tensor coprojection. -/
noncomputable def tensorOverlapBase :
    Spec (.of L) ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))

/-- The two tensor coprojections have the same composite to the challenge base. -/
lemma tensorOverlapInl_comp_base :
    tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L) ≫ tensorOverlapBase (k := k) (L := L) =
      tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L) ≫ tensorOverlapBase (k := k) (L := L) := by
  simp only [tensorOverlapInl, tensorOverlapInr, tensorOverlapBase]
  rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← Spec.map_comp]
  have h := tensorInl_comp_ofId (k := k) (A := k) (B := L)
  congr 1
  ext x
  exact DFunLike.congr_fun h x

/-! ## The presheaf comparison -/

/-- Rebase an L-side Picard functor along one tensor coprojection, then identify it
with the fixed k-side functor through theta and the common composite to `Spec k`. -/
noncomputable def tensorOverlapCommon
    (f : Spec (.of (L ⊗[k] L)) ⟶ Spec (.of L)) :
    (Over.map f).op ⋙ pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C) ≅
      (Over.map (f ≫ tensorOverlapBase (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
        pic0TypeFunctor C :=
  Functor.isoWhiskerLeft (Over.map f).op (pic0ThetaType k L C) ≪≫
    (Functor.associator (Over.map f).op (Over.map (tensorOverlapBase (k := k) (L := L))).op
      (pic0TypeFunctor C)).symm ≪≫
    (Functor.isoWhiskerRight
      (NatIso.op (Over.mapComp f (tensorOverlapBase (k := k) (L := L))))
      (pic0TypeFunctor C)).symm

/-- The canonical natural isomorphism between the two tensor-coprojection pullback
presheaves. -/
noncomputable def tensorOverlapTheta :
    (Over.map (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
        pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C) ≅
      (Over.map (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
        pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C) :=
  tensorOverlapCommon (C := C) (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L)) ≪≫
    eqToIso (congrArg
      (fun g => (Over.map g).op ⋙ pic0TypeFunctor C)
      (tensorOverlapInl_comp_base (k := k) (L := L))) ≪≫
    (tensorOverlapCommon (C := C) (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))).symm

/-! ## Pullback representations and the canonical scheme isomorphism -/

variable {J : Over (Spec (.of L))}

/-- The representation pulled back along the first tensor coprojection. -/
noncomputable def tensorOverlapRepInl
    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).RepresentableBy J) :
    ((Over.map (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
      pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).RepresentableBy
        ((Over.pullback (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))).obj J) :=
  Functor.RepresentableBy.ofLeftAdjoint
    (Over.mapPullbackAdj (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))) rep

/-- The representation pulled back along the second tensor coprojection. -/
noncomputable def tensorOverlapRepInr
    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).RepresentableBy J) :
    ((Over.map (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
      pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).RepresentableBy
        ((Over.pullback (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))).obj J) :=
  Functor.RepresentableBy.ofLeftAdjoint
    (Over.mapPullbackAdj (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))) rep

/-- The canonical representing-scheme isomorphism on the double tensor overlap. -/
noncomputable def tensorOverlapIso
    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).RepresentableBy J) :
    (Over.pullback (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))).obj J ≅
      (Over.pullback (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))).obj J :=
  Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIsoOfIso
    (tensorOverlapRepInl rep) (tensorOverlapRepInr rep)
    (tensorOverlapTheta (C := C))

set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
-- The expanded Over pullback comparison crosses several categorical
-- functors; its definitional check exceeds Lean's default heartbeat budget.
/-- Universal-element characterization of the tensor-overlap comparison. -/
theorem tensorOverlapIso_homEquiv
    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).RepresentableBy J)
    {T : Over (Spec (.of (L ⊗[k] L)))}
    (f : T ⟶ (Over.pullback (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))).obj J) :
    (tensorOverlapRepInr rep).homEquiv
        (f ≫ (tensorOverlapIso rep).hom) =
      (tensorOverlapTheta (C := C)).hom.app (Opposite.op T)
        ((tensorOverlapRepInl rep).homEquiv f) :=
  Functor.RepresentableBy.homEquiv_uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_hom
    (tensorOverlapRepInl rep) (tensorOverlapRepInr rep)
    (tensorOverlapTheta (C := C)) f

end AlgebraicGeometry

  1492	What is *not* free is the **typing**, and this is the third time this lane has paid for it: the
  1493	keystones are spelled at localization instance packs (`[Algebra R (S i)]`,
  1494	`[IsLocalization.Away (g i) (S i)]`) while the vehicle's compatibility is spelled at

  1497	change does not compile, and a port that does is mechanical.
  1498	
  1499	### 9.3 The comparison is a natural transformation, and that is the form a consumer substitutes
  1500	
  1501	`divFamZarToAffVehicle` (ADDENDUM 6) was componentwise: it said the two carriers agree at each
  1502	affine open. That is not what a consumer holding a section over a general test wants. It wants to
  1503	replace `divFunctor` by `divFunctorAff` and **keep its restriction equations** — which is
  1504	naturality, and which is what `divFunctorToAff` now provides.
  1505	
  1506	The proof needs no gluing: the componentwise image of the chart-typed glued value already has the
  1507	*widened* pullback property, because `DivFamZar.toAff_mapAlgHom` turns each clause of the
  1508	chart-typed `mapVal_spec` into the corresponding widened clause, and widened uniqueness
  1509	(`divFamZarAff.mapVal_eq_of`) closes it.
  1510	
  1511	Direction: **old → new only**, and that is content, not omission. By ADDENDUM 3 §2 / ADDENDUM 4
  1512	§4.3 there is a straddling divisor at every genus `≥ 2` that no fixed pair of `P¹` charts can
  1513	confine, so no transformation back can exist.

  1640	including the control that must fire*. Cause: a producer builds the structure with

summary: 'DECIDED 2026-07-27: choose R1, coordinate twists, as the architecture-preserving
  widening. Declaration-level audits reject R2 as a much wider FinCoverData/support-principalization
  refactor and R3 as a replacement of the established divisor representation layer.
  p1-aut and the infinite-field fibre-avoidance branch are landed. CORRECTION AFTER
  GROUND REVIEW: a finite Galois extension of a finite field is still finite, so it
  cannot instantiate the landed Infinite-field theorem. The arbitrary-field completion
  is now tracked by finite-field-avoid: prove a finite-cardinality avoidance lemma,
  bound the fibre-support image by degree g, choose a sufficiently large finite Galois
  extension, and then use the existing Galois-descent substrate. The proposed in-place
  cert-relocalize refactor is rejected because every DivRepGlobalData classifier is
  fixed in pi; its replacement is the outer twist-atlas row, which retains each fixed-twist
  classifier and glues those charts on common divisor loci.'
